geochron.geochronnotes: Date was just below Ambrosia rise, which ought to be ca. 100 BP (AD 1850).
δ13C not measured because of unusually high nitrogen content of the gas produced on combustion.
Date should be good (no correction for old carbon required). Date is on material from trash layer. Base of lake sediment is 1725 cm, with estimated age of ca. 12000 BP.

chronology.notes: Chron uses 11 radiocarbon dates plus the top (-25 BP, 650 cm). Five levels above the Ambrosia-rise (662-702 cm) have been corrected for compaction (see Grimm 1981). Because the radiocarbon date at the Ambrosia-rise (630±55) is ca. 530 years too old and because a hardwater effect is expected, all radiocarbon dates except the basal date have been corrected for a 530 yr reservoir. The basal date on wood in the trash layer should not be subject to hardwater error and was not corrected. The base of the lake sediment was assigned an age 60 years younger than the trash layer.

chronology.notes: Chron uses adjusted radiocarbon dates from NAPD 1 calibated with Calib 5.0.2 using the INTCAL04 calibration curve.

Based on the IntCal13 calibration curve. The ages below 1725 cm were interplated from the Bacon age at 1725 cm to the median of the calibrated age 13930 of the 12060±125 radiocarbon date, which was in the trash layer.
